text.p: Med oil products were stronger on Thursday, traders said.
Gas oil climed $3.75 a tonne in line with September IPE, which closed at $173.75 on healthy U.S. gasoline.

A European refiner and a trader both continued to try to offload cargoes of low sulphur diesel at a weaker Septemebr IPE +$1.50, with the apparent intention of working an arbitrage to NWE on the back of the lower quote.
Both firms have up to six stems to offer. While traders say Russian appears competitive against Italian heating oil a lack of buying interest slowed talk.
High sulphur fuel oil was offered stronger with little supply seen and no offers from refiners.

A refiner said it turned down a bid at $84 fob for a large cargo to go to Cuba or Singapore, adding an end month cargo of 25kt it has would be probably be sold to a term contractor at about fob high Med +$1.25/$1.50.
The refiner said traders were showing interest in larger sized cargoes, about 80,000 tonnes, rather than medium-sized ones -- showing an open arb to the Far East and other destinations.
Low sulphur was notionally stronger at the $109/$111 mark with traders saying most of the Black Sea material has already been sold.
One trader said he had bid $109.50 cif for a prompt cargo of low sulphur into Italy for August 20 arrival and was also seeking a cargo of 30,000 tonnes into Lebanon.
"The (Med) market is definitely stronger, it is stronger in the United States and swaps are higher (in NWE)," the trader said.
Naphtha was a touch firmer in line with gains seen in northwest Europe. An Alexandria cargo was sold on Wednesday at the equivalent of around $196-197 cif NWE.
Gasoline supplies remain tight and hard to source and the possiblity of drawing NWE cargoes southwards looks more tenuous with U.S. buyers taking up to 150,000 tonnes of NWE material.
"Italian and French buyers will have to compete against American buyers if they want to attract cargoes into the Med," said one trader.
